To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the environmental performance of a novel AM process, Fast Mask Image Projection (MIP) Stereolithography (SL) was evaluated using a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology, (ii) process energy was the main contributor to environmental impacts, (iii) the environmental impact increased with the complexity and size of the part, (iv) a mathematical model for process energy consumption was developed, and (v) the model was validated using experimental data.
The Fast MIP SL additive manufacturing process is an energy-intensive process.
